passages.title: Information Security & Acceptable Use
passages.text:
Never use a personal laptop to store, open or work on Ridgeline project files, whether at home, in the office or travelling.
This applies even to a quick look at a drawing or a short edit to a calculation. Personal laptops are outside IT's management, so Ridgeline cannot protect, track or wipe the files on them. If you don't have a Ridgeline laptop with you when you need one, ask IT about a loan device rather than using your own.

passages.title: Equipment & Home-Office Stipend
passages.text:
Personal laptops are not reimbursed, and they may not hold Ridgeline project files (RSE-SEC-01 §3.3). Use the Ridgeline laptop you were issued for all project work.
Personal accessories such as your own headphones or keyboard may be used with Ridgeline equipment, but they are not reimbursed outside the stipend in §2. If your Ridgeline laptop isn't suitable for your work, ask IT for a replacement rather than using a personal machine.

passages.title: Equipment & Home-Office Stipend
passages.text:
Every employee gets a standard kit from IT: a laptop, two monitors and a headset. Field/site-based employees also get a rugged tablet for site work. IT has your equipment ready before your first day (RSE-ONB-01 §1). Interns receive the standard kit for the length of their internship.
The kit is set up by IT with the software and security settings you need. Office-hybrid employees keep their laptop with them and use shared monitors on their anchor days; ask IT if you need monitors at home too. Specialist equipment, such as a high-performance workstation for analysis or modelling, is arranged through your manager and IT.

passages.title: Information Security & Acceptable Use
passages.text:
Notify IT Security at least 5 working days before you start working from another country. IT Security will check that your device and access are set up for the destination, and may issue a travel laptop for the trip. This applies in addition to the HR review in RSE-LOC-01 §3.
Some destinations have rules on encryption or on carrying certain data, and some client agreements forbid access from particular countries. IT Security checks these before you go. Don't take Client Restricted paper documents abroad, and keep your devices with you while travelling. Business trips abroad follow the same notification rule when you will work on Ridgeline systems while away.

passages.title: Information Security & Acceptable Use
passages.text:
Confidential and Client Restricted data may only be stored or worked on using company-managed devices: the laptops and tablets Ridgeline issues, which IT keeps encrypted and up to date.
Don't disable security software, change device settings that IT manages, or let anyone else use your Ridgeline device. Install updates when prompted; IT may restart devices that fall too far behind.

passages.title: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
passages.text:
Your remote workspace must meet the security requirements in RSE-SEC-01 §5: use the VPN, keep screens private and never print Client Restricted documents at home.
Work in a space where others can't overhear confidential calls or see your screen, and lock your device when you step away. Use only company-managed devices for project work.

passages.title: Equipment & Home-Office Stipend
passages.text:
Office-hybrid employees can claim a one-time home-office stipend of $250 for their remote days.
Suitable items include a desk chair, a monitor arm, a desk lamp or a keyboard. The stipend can't be used for furniture unrelated to work or for general household items.

passages.title: Information Security & Acceptable Use
passages.text:
Report a lost or stolen Ridgeline device, or a personal phone enrolled in mobile management, to IT Security within 1 hour of noticing, so the device can be locked or wiped.
Report it even if you think the device may turn up again. If it was stolen, report the theft to the local police as well and give IT the report reference.

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.section_heading: Adding personal days to a trip
passages.text:
You may add personal days to a business trip. Personal days are taken as PTO under the Paid Time Off Policy (RSE-PTO-01), and the costs of the personal days are yours (RSE-EXP-01 §6).
Request the PTO in the usual way, with the usual notice and approval. Your holiday calendar is still your home office's calendar while you travel. Adding a few personal days doesn't turn a business trip into temporary remote work, provided you don't work on those days.

passages.title: Equipment & Home-Office Stipend
passages.text: Remote-approved employees can also claim $50 per month toward home internet. Office-hybrid employees cannot claim internet costs.
